 THIS MFA IS FILED U/S 173(1) OF MV ACT AGAINST THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 04.11.2017 PASSED IN MVC NO.582/2016 ON THE FILE OF THE XIII ADDITIONAL JUDGE, COURT OF SMALL CAUSES AND MEMBER MACT, BENGALURU (SCCH-15), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MR JUSTICE N S SANJAY GOWDA  -4-  NC: 2024:KHC:43753  MFA No. 1442 of 2018  C/W MFA No. 1441 of 2018  ORAL JUDGMENT 1. The claimants, being dissatisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal and also exoneration of liability of the insurer, are in appeal. 
2. The occurrence of the accident is not in dispute. The Tribunal, however, recorded a finding that the driver of the tanker lorry (which was insured and which was collided with the motorcycle) was not authorized to drive a tanker lorry which was carrying hazardous goods and has, therefore,
absolved the insurance company of all liability and fastened it on the owner. 
3. Learned counsel for the claimants points out that as per the Central Motor Vehicle Rules, 1989 (the 'CMV Rules' for short), for driving a tanker carrying hazardous goods, the only requirement is to possess a license to drive heavy goods vehicle and the driver is required to undertake a course with a specified syllabus and also undergo Refresher Training Course every year. He submits that,
Sathivel vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65579309/
3 NC: 2024:KHC:43753 admittedly, the driver did possess heavy goods vehicle license and the owner himself had produced the Certificate issued by the Indianoil Corporation Limited, which certified that the driver had obtained a Certificate for having undergone a Course in Hazards of Petroleum Products, Safety in Transportation of Petroleum Products by Road, Do's and Don'ts in Transportation, etc.
4. He also points out that the owner had also produced Driver's Refresher Training Course dated 10.04.2016 which indicated that he had participated in a one-day Refresher Training Program as required under Section 14(2) r/w Rule 9 of the CMV Rules and he was thus competent to drive the tanker and the exoneration of liability of the insurer was therefore incorrect.
5. Ex.R2 clearly establishes that the driver of the tanker lorry had undertaken a course and obtained a Training Certificate in relation to transportation of hazardous goods. 
NC: 2024:KHC:43753 6. The Drivers' Refresher Training Course, which was issued by the Karnataka State Transport Department Officers' Association, also indicates that he had participated in a one-day Refresher Training Program as required under Section 14(2) r/w Rule 9 of CMV Rules. 
7. It is therefore clear that the driver of the tanker lorry did possess the necessary certificates to drive a tanker and transport hazardous goods. 
8. In this view of the matter, the exoneration of liability of the insurer cannot be sustained and it is held that the insurer would be responsible for payment of the compensation. 
9. Insofar as the claim for enhancement is concerned, the evidence on record indicates that the claimant in MFA No.1442/2018 had suffered fracture of the right femur shaft and the doctor who was examined has stated that he was having functional disability of 16.75% to the whole NC:
2024:KHC:43753 body. But the Tribunal has taken the whole body disability only at 8%.
10. In my view, taking into consideration that the claimant had suffered a fracture of the right femur shaft, it is appropriate to treat the whole body disability at 15%. 
11. As far as monthly income is concerned, the Tribunal has concluded that the claimant was earning Rs.7,000/- per month. In my view, since there is no evidence to ascertain the actual income,
notional income of Rs.9,000/- has to be applied as per the determination made by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority for accidents of the year 2015. 
12. As the claimant was aged 25 years, a multiplier of '18' will have to be applied. Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.2,91,600/- (Rs.9,000X18X12X15%) towards 'loss of future income'. 
NC: 2024:KHC:43753 Sathivel vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65579309/ 
4 13 . The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'pain and suffering' and Rs.20,000/-
towards 'loss of amenities'. Having regard to the fracture to a major bone, it would be appropriate to enhance the said amounts to Rs.50,000/- under each heads. 
14. A sum of Rs.1,35,000/- awarded towards 'medical expenses' being based on documentary evidence, is affirmed. 
15. The Tribunal has taken the laid-up period as two months. Since the claimant has suffered a fracture to the right foot, it would be appropriate to treat the laid-up period as three months and award a sum of Rs.27,000/- (9,000X3) towards 'loss of income during the laid-up period' as against Rs.14,000/- awarded by the Tribunal. 
16. The claimant was hospitalized for about 15 days. In that view of the matter, the claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards 'Food, nutrition, conveyance NC: 2024:KHC:43753 and attendant charges' as against Rs.10,000/- and 4,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.
17. Consequently, the award of the Tribunal is modified and the claimant in MFA No.1442/2018 would be entitled to the following compensation:
 As awarded As  by the awarded  Sl. Compensation  Tribunal by this  No. under different  Court  Heads (Rs.)
 (Rs.)
 Loss of future 1,21,000 2,91,600  1.
 income  Medical 1,35,000 1,35,000  2.
 expenditure  3. Pain and sufferings 20,000 50,000  4. Loss of amenities 20,000 50,000  Conveyance, food, 14,200 20,000  5. nourishment and  (10,000+4,200)
 attendant charges  Loss of income 14,000 27,000  6. during the laid-up  period  Total 3,24,200 5,73,600 Sathivel vs Shriram General Insurance Co Ltd on 29 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65579309/
5  - 10 -  NC: 2024:KHC:43753 18. Thus, the claimant in MFA No.1442/2018 is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.5,73,600/- as against Rs.3,24,200/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization. 
19. The appeal insofar as the other claimant is concerned, i.e., Mr. Ramaraj in MFA No.1441/2018,
the Tribunal has awarded a global compensation of Rs.25,000/-. 
20. The evidence on record indicates that the claimant had suffered simple injuries for which the claimant had spent a sum of Rs.13,950/- towards treatment. 
21. In my view, it is appropriate to enhance the global compensation from Rs.25,000/- to Rs.40,000/-. 
22. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment. 
23. The disbursement of the compensation amount shall be in terms of the award of the Tribunal. 
- 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:43753 24. These appeals are, accordingly, allowed in part.
